docs.title: USR-ES1 W5500 SPI Ethernet Module - RF201
docs.text: SPI Ethernet module based on WIZnet W5500 chip. Features hardware TCP/IP stack, 10/100 Mbps Ethernet, and integrated magnetics with RJ45 connector. Perfect for adding reliable wired network connectivity to any microcontroller.

docs.title: Key Specifications
docs.text: Parameter Value Chip WIZnet W5500 Ethernet speed 10/100 Mbps (auto-negotiation) Interface SPI (up to 80 MHz) TCP/IP stack Hardware (on-chip) Sockets 8 independent hardware sockets Buffer 32KB (16KB TX + 16KB RX) Supply voltage 3.0V - 3.6V (module: 3.3V or 5V) Current ~132mA (active), ~15mA (power-down) Operating temp -40°C to +85°C Connector RJ45 with integrated magnetics

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Hardware TCP/IP stack: - W5500 chip handles all network protocols in hardware - No software TCP/IP stack needed on MCU - MCU communicates via simple SPI commands - Greatly reduces MCU load and code complexity

Independent sockets: - 8 simultaneous TCP or UDP connections - Each socket has its own buffer - Can act as server, client, or both

docs.title: Pinout (USR-ES1 Module)
docs.text:
USR-ES1 Module
   ____________
  | RJ45       |  Ethernet connector
  |   []       |
  |____________|
   | | | | | | |
   V G S S S S I
   C N C M I N R
   C D K O S T Q
           S O

VCC  = Power (3.3V or 5V)
GND  = Ground
SCK  = SPI Clock
MOSI = SPI Master Out Slave In
MISO = SPI Master In Slave Out
INT  = Interrupt output (optional)
IRQ  = Same as INT (some modules label differently)

Some modules also have: 

RST  = Reset input (active LOW)
CS   = Chip Select (sometimes called SS)

docs.title: Typical Wiring (ESP32)
docs.text:
ESP32           USR-ES1 (W5500)
-----           ---------------
3.3V   -------> VCC
GND    -------> GND
GPIO18 -------> SCK
GPIO23 -------> MOSI
GPIO19 -------> MISO
GPIO5  -------> CS (or SS)
GPIO4  -------> RST (optional)

Ethernet cable: Connect to router/switch with standard Cat5e/Cat6 cable.

docs.title: Example Code (ESP32)
docs.text:
// ESP32 + W5500 Ethernet
// Install: Ethernet library (built-in)
#include <SPI.h>
#include <Ethernet.h>

#define CS_PIN 5

byte mac[] = {0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF, 0xFE, 0xED};

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);

  Ethernet.init(CS_PIN);

  Serial.println("Connecting to network...");

  if (Ethernet.begin(mac)) {  // DHCP
    Serial.println("DHCP OK!");
  } else {
    Serial.println("DHCP failed!");
    return;
  }

  Serial.print("IP address: ");
  Serial.println(Ethernet.localIP());
}

void loop() {
  // Check link status
  if (Ethernet.linkStatus() == LinkOFF) {
    Serial.println("Ethernet cable disconnected");
  }

  delay(1000);
}

docs.title: Static IP Configuration
docs.text:
void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  Ethernet.init(CS_PIN);

  // Set static IP instead of DHCP
  IPAddress ip(192, 168, 1, 100);
  IPAddress dns(192, 168, 1, 1);
  IPAddress gateway(192, 168, 1, 1);
  IPAddress subnet(255, 255, 255, 0);

  Ethernet.begin(mac, ip, dns, gateway, subnet);

  Serial.print("IP: ");
  Serial.println(Ethernet.localIP());
}

docs.title: Web Server Example
docs.text:
EthernetServer server(80);

void setup() {
  // ... (Ethernet init code)
  server.begin();
  Serial.println("Web server started");
}

void loop() {
  EthernetClient client = server.available();

  if (client) {
    Serial.println("New client connected");

    while (client.connected()) {
      if (client.available()) {
        char c = client.read();

        // Simple HTTP response
        if (c == '\n') {
          client.println("HTTP/1.1 200 OK");
          client.println("Content-Type: text/html");
          client.println();
          client.println("<h1>Hello from ESP32 + W5500!</h1>");
          client.stop();
          break;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: HTTP Client (GET Request)
docs.text:
void loop() {
  EthernetClient client;

  if (client.connect("example.com", 80)) {
    Serial.println("Connected to server");

    client.println("GET / HTTP/1.1");
    client.println("Host: example.com");
    client.println("Connection: close");
    client.println();

    while (client.connected()) {
      if (client.available()) {
        char c = client.read();
        Serial.write(c);
      }
    }

    client.stop();
  } else {
    Serial.println("Connection failed");
  }

  delay(10000);  // Wait 10 seconds before next request
}

docs.title: MAC Address
docs.text:
W5500 doesn't have built-in MAC address. You must assign one:

// Use random but locally-administered MAC
byte mac[] = {
  0x02,  // Locally administered (bit 1 of first byte = 1)
  random(0xFF),
  random(0xFF),
  random(0xFF),
  random(0xFF),
  random(0xFF)
};

Or use fixed MAC (ensure uniqueness on your network): 

byte mac[] = {0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF, 0xFE, 0xED};

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
Hardware TCP/IP: - No software stack needed - Reduces MCU code size - Offloads network processing

8 independent sockets: - Multiple simultaneous connections - Mix TCP and UDP - Server + client at same time

Auto-negotiation: - Automatic 10/100 Mbps speed detection - Auto-MDI/MDIX (crossover cable not needed)

Low MCU load: - Hardware handles protocols - SPI communication only - MCU can focus on application

Integrated magnetics: - Direct RJ45 connection - No external transformers needed - Compact design

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
1. No built-in MAC: Must assign MAC address in code
  2. 3.3V logic: W5500 is 3.3V - check module has level shifting for 5V MCUs
  3. SPI speed: W5500 supports up to 80 MHz, but long wires may require slower speed
  4. Power consumption: ~132mA when active (consider for battery projects)
  5. Cable required: Obviously needs Ethernet cable to router/switch
  6. Library compatibility: Use Ethernet library (not Ethernet2 or Ethernet3)

docs.title: W5500 vs WiFi
docs.text:
Feature W5500 Ethernet (RF201) ESP32 WiFi Connection Wired (cable) Wireless Reliability Excellent Good (interference possible) Speed 10/100 Mbps Up to 150 Mbps (real: ~20-50) Latency Very low Higher (variable) Power ~132mA ~160-260mA Setup Plug-and-play (DHCP) Need SSID/password Mobility Fixed location Mobile

Use Ethernet when: - Reliability critical - Fixed installation - No WiFi interference concerns - PoE power desired - Industrial environments

Use WiFi when: - Mobility needed - No cable access - Temporary installation - Many devices (no switch ports)

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Home automation: Wired backbone for smart home hubs.

Industrial control: PLCs, automation controllers, factory equipment.

Server applications: Data logging, web servers, MQTT brokers.

Security systems: IP cameras, access control, alarm panels.

PoE devices: With PoE module, power + data over single cable.

Arduino Ethernet: Add wired network to Arduino boards.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No link (link LED off): - Check cable connection - Verify cable is good (test with PC) - Check both ends connected - Try different cable

DHCP fails: - Router DHCP enabled? - Check MAC address is valid - Try static IP - Check SPI wiring (SCK/MOSI/MISO/CS)

Can't connect to internet: - Can ping gateway? (use Ethernet.gatewayIP()) - DNS working? (try IP address instead of hostname) - Check firewall settings

Intermittent connection: - SPI wires too long (add shorter wires) - Reduce SPI clock speed - Check power supply (needs clean 3.3V) - Add decoupling capacitor (100nF) near VCC pin

docs.title: RF-5V 433MHz Wireless Transceiver Module - RF202
docs.text: Simple 433MHz wireless transceiver module for point-to-point communication. Features UART interface for serial data transmission over air. Perfect for wireless sensors, remote control, and simple telemetry applications.

docs.title: Key Specifications
docs.text: Parameter Value Frequency 433 MHz (ISM band) Range ~100m (open air, line-of-sight) Interface UART (serial) Baud rate Configurable (1200-115200 bps typical) Supply voltage 5V DC Current ~20mA (RX), ~35mA (TX) Modulation ASK/OOK (typical) Operating temp -20°C to +70°C

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Wireless UART: - Transparent serial passthrough - Data in on TX pin → transmitted over air - Received data → output on RX pin - Like invisible wire between two microcontrollers

433 MHz ISM band: - License-free frequency - Good penetration through walls - Longer range than 2.4 GHz - Less crowded than WiFi

docs.title: Pinout
docs.text:
RF-5V Module
    ___
   |~~~| Antenna
   | R |
   | F |
   |___|
   | | | |
   V G R T
   C N X X
   C D

VCC = Power (5V)
GND = Ground
RX  = Receive data (input to module)
TX  = Transmit data (output from module)

Some modules also have: 

EN  = Enable pin (pull HIGH to enable)
SET = Configuration mode pin

docs.title: Typical Wiring (ESP32)
docs.text:
MCU             RF-5V
---             -----
5V     -------> VCC
GND    -------> GND
TX     -------> RX (MCU transmits to RF module)
RX     -------> TX (MCU receives from RF module)

Note: Use level shifter if MCU is 3.3V logic (ESP32 RX is 3.3V tolerant but TX may need shifting to 5V).

docs.title: Example Code (ESP32)
docs.text:
// ESP32 + RF-5V Transceiver
// Using Serial2 (GPIO16=RX2, GPIO17=TX2)
#define RXD2 16
#define TXD2 17

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);   // Debug
  Serial2.begin(9600, SERIAL_8N1, RXD2, TXD2);  // RF module

  Serial.println("RF-5V Wireless Ready");
}

void loop() {
  // Send data
  if (Serial.available()) {
    char c = Serial.read();
    Serial2.write(c);  // Transmit over RF
    Serial.print("Sent: ");
    Serial.println(c);
  }

  // Receive data
  if (Serial2.available()) {
    char c = Serial2.read();
    Serial.print("Received: ");
    Serial.println(c);
  }
}

docs.title: Wireless Sensor Example
docs.text:
Transmitter (sensor side): 

void loop() {
  float temperature = 25.3;
  int humidity = 65;

  // Send data packet
  Serial2.print("T:");
  Serial2.print(temperature);
  Serial2.print(",H:");
  Serial2.println(humidity);

  delay(5000);  // Send every 5 seconds
}

Receiver (base station): 

void loop() {
  if (Serial2.available()) {
    String data = Serial2.readStringUntil('\n');
    Serial.print("Sensor data: ");
    Serial.println(data);

    // Parse data: "T:25.3,H:65"
    int tIndex = data.indexOf("T:");
    int hIndex = data.indexOf("H:");

    if (tIndex >= 0 && hIndex >= 0) {
      float temp = data.substring(tIndex + 2, hIndex - 1).toFloat();
      int hum = data.substring(hIndex + 2).toInt();

      Serial.printf("Temperature: %.1f°C, Humidity: %d%%\n", temp, hum);
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Remote Control Example
docs.text:
Transmitter (remote): 

#define BUTTON_1 25
#define BUTTON_2 26

void loop() {
  if (digitalRead(BUTTON_1) == LOW) {
    Serial2.println("CMD:LIGHT_ON");
    delay(200);  // Debounce
  }

  if (digitalRead(BUTTON_2) == LOW) {
    Serial2.println("CMD:LIGHT_OFF");
    delay(200);
  }

  delay(50);
}

Receiver (controller): 

#define RELAY_PIN 27

void loop() {
  if (Serial2.available()) {
    String cmd = Serial2.readStringUntil('\n');

    if (cmd == "CMD:LIGHT_ON") {
      digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, HIGH);
      Serial.println("Light turned ON");
    } else if (cmd == "CMD:LIGHT_OFF") {
      digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, LOW);
      Serial.println("Light turned OFF");
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
Simple UART interface: - Transparent serial passthrough - No complex protocols - Works with any MCU

Good range: - ~100m line-of-sight - Better than IR - Works through walls

Low cost: - Very cheap modules - No licensing fees - Easy to source

Low power: - Good for battery applications - Sleep modes available - Low RX current

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
1. 5V only: Module requires 5V power (not 3.3V)
  2. No handshaking: No acknowledgment of received data
  3. Packet loss: RF interference can cause data loss
  4. No error correction: Corrupted data not detected
  5. Half-duplex: Can't transmit and receive simultaneously
  6. Range varies: Obstacles, interference reduce range significantly
  7. Antenna needed: Many modules need external antenna for good range

docs.title: Adding Reliability
docs.text:
Simple packet format: 

void sendPacket(String data) {
  // Add start marker and checksum
  String packet = "<" + data + ">";
  Serial2.println(packet);
}

String receivePacket() {
  static String buffer = "";

  while (Serial2.available()) {
    char c = Serial2.read();
    buffer += c;

    if (c == '>') {  // End marker
      int start = buffer.indexOf('<');
      if (start >= 0) {
        String packet = buffer.substring(start + 1, buffer.length() - 1);
        buffer = "";
        return packet;
      }
    }
  }

  return "";
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Some modules support AT commands for configuration:

void setup() {
  Serial2.begin(9600);

  // Enter config mode (varies by module)
  // Pull SET pin LOW or send special command

  // Example AT commands (module-specific):
  Serial2.println("AT+ADDR=01");     // Set address
  Serial2.println("AT+BAUD=4");      // Set baud rate
  Serial2.println("AT+POWER=20");    // Set TX power (dBm)

  delay(500);
}

Check module datasheet for specific AT commands.

docs.title: RF-5V vs WiFi
docs.text:
Feature RF-5V (RF202) WiFi (ESP32) Range ~100m ~50-100m Setup Simple UART WiFi credentials needed Internet No (local only) Yes (via router) Power ~20-35mA ~160-260mA Cost $1-2 $3-5 (ESP32) Data rate Low (kbps) High (Mbps)

Use RF-5V when: - Simple point-to-point needed - No internet required - Low power critical - Very low cost needed

Use WiFi when: - Internet connectivity needed - Higher data rate required - Network infrastructure available

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Wireless sensors: Temperature, humidity, motion sensors without wires.

Remote control: Control lights, relays, motors wirelessly.

Telemetry: Send sensor data from remote locations.

Home automation: Simple wireless control without WiFi.

Weather station: Outdoor sensor to indoor display.

Wireless doorbell: Transmitter button to receiver chime.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No communication: - Check baud rate matches both sides - Verify TX/RX not swapped - Check 5V power adequate - Antenna connected?

Short range: - Add/improve antenna - Check for RF interference - Obstacles blocking signal - Increase TX power (if configurable)

Corrupted data: - Reduce baud rate - Add error checking (checksums) - Reduce distance - Use packet format with delimiters

Intermittent connection: - RF interference (try different channel if module supports it) - Power supply unstable - Antenna loose

docs.text: Aliases: TTGO LoRa32, WiFi LoRa 32, Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 Category: MC Family: ESP32

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text:
• CPU: Dual-core Tensilica Xtensa LX6 @ 240 MHz (ESP32)
  • Memory: 520 KB SRAM, 4 MB Flash (32Mbit)
  • Computing Power: Up to 600 DMIPS
  • Wireless: WiFi 802.11 b/g/n, Bluetooth 4.2 BR/EDR + BLE
  • LoRa: SX1276/SX1278 chipset
  • Frequency Bands: 433 MHz, 868 MHz, 915 MHz
  • LoRa Range: Up to 2.8 km (open field)
  • Receiver Sensitivity: -139 dBm @ SF12, 125 kHz
  • TX Power: 19.5 dBm @ 11b, 16.5 dBm @ 11g, 15.5 dBm @ 11n
  • Display: 0.96" OLED (I2C)
  • Operating Voltage: 3.3-7V
  • USB Adapter: CP2102
  • I/O Voltage: 3.3V

docs.title: Arduino Configuration
docs.text:
• Board: "TTGO LoRa32-OLED" or "Heltec WiFi LoRa 32"
  • FQBN: esp32:esp32:ttgo-lora32 or esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32
